clue.text: Backing for picture always around method for achieving success

indicators.note: backing means the whole assembled piece is read from the end to the start
around says the word for always wraps the picture word

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: Advice about framing a picture, oddly sandwiched with a phrase about the secret of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picture always around' means the picture word is wrapped by the poetic word for always; 'Backing' then reads the result from end to start.
explanation.definitionFit: A formula that reliably leads to a result is called a recipe, as in a recipe for success.

clue.text: Wolfish party gets support from us in Paris

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, which props it up

parts.note: a rave is a wild party
nous is French for us

explanation.surface: A hungry party is held up by help from Parisians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets support from' places RAVE above NOUS in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfish appetite is greedy and starving, a synonym for extremely hungry.

clue.text: Some Americans in prison

indicators.note: some says only a part of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: A remark that a few Americans are behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' pulls the run from the middle of 'Americans'; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is slang, chiefly American, for a jail.

clue.text: Stick around — I am providing a diversion

indicators.note: around tells us the glue word goes outside the other piece

parts.note: paste is a glue, so to paste is to stick
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone hangs about saying they're there to entertain.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby that diverts or amuses you is a synonym for a diversion.

clue.text: Waterway at which nobleman from France boarded

indicators.note: boarded means got on to, so the pieces go inside the word at

parts.note: que is French for which, the French reading carried by from France
a duc is a French duke

explanation.surface: Asks where a French nobleman got aboard a boat on a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from France' does duty for both French words, the relative pronoun and the noble title.
explanation.definitionFit: An aqueduct is a channel or bridge carrying water, so a kind of waterway.

clue.text: Inquest entails handling that's perfect

indicators.note: handling suggests the letters are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A coroner's hearing involves dealing with something flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handling' rearranges INQUEST ENTAILS. The OCR text reads 'per-feet' for 'perfect'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is the purest example of its kind is ideal, a synonym of perfect.

clue.text: Strange stuff from the east — coax it out

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for east

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Advice to coax something weird out from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges COAX IT into XOTICA, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are unusual, foreign or bizarre objects, so strange stuff.

clue.text: Seizing risky opportunity made one general

indicators.note: seizing means grasping, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to unify is to make into one, so unified means made one
a spec is a speculation, a risky venture

explanation.surface: Grabbing a gamble got a soldier promoted to general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like a soldier in the surface, but it is the adjective meaning vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Unspecified means not detailed, vague, a sense of general.

clue.text: Worry interrupting attempt to reach agreement

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the worry word goes inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to eat, as in what's eating you, is to worry

explanation.surface: Anxiety breaks into an effort to strike a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal pact between states, a type of agreement.

clue.text: Sleeping toddler we had to shake

indicators.note: to shake something is to jumble it, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: We had to rock the little one to get it to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shake' rearranges TODDLER WE HAD TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead to the world is an idiom for fast asleep, a sense of sleeping.

clue.text: Ancient statue, damaged, lies unmoved

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An old statue is broken yet stays still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges LIES UNMOVED; the famous statue is itself armless, which fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venus de Milo is a Hellenistic Greek sculpture, an example of an ancient statue.

clue.text: Girl to take to court

definitions.meaning: a girl's name, short for Susan
to bring a legal action against someone

explanation.definitionFit: Sue is a female first name, and to sue means to start a lawsuit.

clue.text: Mollycoddled little orphan in a state

indicators.note: in places the orphan's name inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: ND is the abbreviation for North Dakota, a US state
Little Orphan Annie is a US comic-strip character

explanation.surface: A pampered child is described as a little orphan in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a state' looks like a fluster, but it is a US state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To nanny someone is to fuss over them, so nannied means overprotected or pampered.

clue.text: Canoodle endlessly, sentimental and dead magical

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the cuddling word is dropped

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle, to canoodle
romantic means sentimental

explanation.surface: Kissing and cuddling, soppy and dead magic, a gothic love scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts K from NECK.
explanation.definitionFit: Necromancy is magic involving communication with the dead.

clue.text: Spear I had found in river

indicators.note: found in says one piece is placed inside the river

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls finding a spear in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, as carried by Neptune.

clue.text: A variety of albums I connect with Harriet's book

indicators.note: a variety means a mixture, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A music fan links several records to a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A variety of' rearranges ALBUMS I CONNECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Harriet Beecher Stowe wrote this anti-slavery novel of 1852.

clue.text: In extremely good nick, I agree

definitions.meaning: in very good health or condition
a phrase of assent, like all right then

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase can mean in fine health, and it is also said to agree to something. Good nick is British for good condition.

clue.text: Listen to golfers' warning: "We will hit off the tee with all-round power"

indicators.note: listen to signals that the words must be heard rather than read

parts.words: golfers' warning: "We will hit off the tee
parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout, we will is we'll, and to drive is to hit off the tee

explanation.surface: Golfers shout a warning before teeing off with great power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listen to' gives FORE, WE'LL DRIVE spoken, which sounds like the vehicle term. Golfers shout fore to warn of a flying ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle with drive to all its wheels has power delivered all round.

clue.text: Climbing tree without one instance of falling back

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top
without means the letter for one is removed

parts.note: an espalier is a fruit tree trained flat against a wall
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Climbing a tree without one slip, a fall averted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes I from ESPALIER, giving ESPALER, and 'Climbing' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a return to illness or bad ways, a falling back.

clue.text: Epitaph penned by divine — lines not requiring subsequent smoothing

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the epitaph goes inside

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a crossword abbreviation for a divine, a clergyman
RIP, rest in peace, is a common epitaph
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the lines

explanation.surface: A clergyman writes an epitaph, about lines needing no polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' for railway is a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Drip-dry clothes are hung up wet and need no ironing afterwards.

clue.text: Elevated knight is old underworld boss

indicators.note: in a down clue elevated means the whole run reads upwards

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: A promoted knight turns out to be an ancient lord of the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' turns SIRISO upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the Egyptian god of the dead and ruler of the afterlife.

clue.text: Superficial justice.

definitions.meaning: Justice ..., a country judge in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2

explanation.definitionFit: The word means lacking depth, and it is the name of a Shakespearean justice of the peace.

clue.text: Further, they have introduced really dedicated, likeable youth leaders

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of each word are taken

parts.words: they have introduced really dedicated, likeable youth

explanation.surface: Moreover, the organisers have brought in keen, pleasant youth leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the first letter of each word from 'they' to 'youth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirdly introduces a next point in a list, as further or moreover does.

clue.text: Tedious routine, but deer find it exciting

definitions.meaning: a dull groove one is stuck in

explanation.definitionFit: A rut is a monotonous routine, and also the period when stags are in heat.

clue.text: Scheme to reduce congestion gets Sam out of the city in dignity

indicators.note: in says the trimmed city goes inside the dignity word

parts.note: pride means self-respect, dignity

indicators.note: out of says Sam is taken away from the city name

parts.note: Samarkand is an ancient city in Uzbekistan
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sam leaves town with his dignity intact.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is the Silk Road city in Uzbekistan; removing Sam from its start leaves the piece that goes inside dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: Park and ride schemes let drivers leave cars outside town and take a bus in, easing traffic.

clue.text: Hostelry, one given new name

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pub, a single one renamed.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub or small hotel, which is what a hostelry is.

clue.text: Attempt to get moisture from pips, we hear, turns out well

indicators.note: we hear signals the words are judged by sound

parts.words: Attempt to get moisture from pips
parts.note: to suck seeds is to try drawing juice from pips

explanation.surface: Sucking the juice from pips works out nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns SUCK SEEDS into the near-identical sounding verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed is to have a good outcome, so it turns out well.

clue.text: Henry, manly sort, produces a book

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: sort as a verb means arrange, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A macho Henry brings out a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' rearranges MANLY into YMNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymnal is a hymn book used in church services.
